messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: page fired -> PD#INC-4578: synth-canary-eu-west repeated failures (5m window) <https://pagerduty.example/INC-4578|open>
pagerduty-bot: Alert details: check=synth-canary-eu-west, metric=latency_5xx_rate, region=eu-west, severity=critical, count=7
anju (oncall): ACK: I'm on it. pinging infra + SRE. @carlos can you take a look if you have bandwidth? :wave:
carlos (sre): Oncall handoff noted. Looking at prober dashboards now. Can you grab the latest prober logs from eu-west-prober-2? I want the tail for the last 10m.
anju (oncall): running:
```
kubectl -n synthetic logs deploy/eu-west-prober-2 --since=10m | sed -n '1,200p'
```
anju (oncall): logs show repeated TLS handshake timeouts and a bunch of `dial tcp 10.12.4.9:443: i/o timeout` errors. Also seeing `upstream reset by peer` about the same time.
carlos (sre): hmmm. Could be network egress flapping or a backend auth rotation. Mei, any deploys/rotation in eu-west around 17:01 UTC? @mei
mei (product): No app deploys from product in last hour. There was an infra change yesterday afternoon to the egress firewall but it was scoped to apac only. I'm checking the infra changelog.
ops-runbook-bot: Runbook snippet: If synth-canary fails with TLS/dial errors: 1) check prober pod restarts, 2) check NAT/gw logs, 3) verify backend cert expiry, 4) consider temporary suppress of PD pages.
anju (oncall): prober pods are stable, no restarts in last 30m. NAT gateway metrics show a spike in connection resets in eu-west-1 at 17:02:30 UTC.
carlos (sre): Good call. Can you curl one of the canaries directly from a control-plane node to confirm? e.g.
```
# from control plane in eu-west
curl -v https://synth-canary-eu-west.healthcheck.internal/ -H 'Host: synth-canary' --connect-timeout 5
```
anju (oncall): curl shows `* TCP_NODELAY set` then `* connect to 10.12.4.9 port 443 failed: Connection timed out` repeatedly.
mei (product): Customer impact: none directly user-visible (these are synthetic checks) but they cover upstream routing and could mask real outages. We should avoid a noisy pagestorm while we triage.
carlos (sre): Plan: 1) suppress PD escalation for this check to stop repeated pages (temporary, 15m), 2) continue triage, 3) if network spike subsides, re-enable; 4) if not, failover synthetic traffic to eu-central and open a ticket to infra.
anju (oncall): suppressing now.
```
# pdctl (internal)
pdctl incidents suppress INC-4578 --duration 15m --reason "investigating network instability, suppress duplicate pages"
```
incident-bot: PagerDuty: suppression applied for INC-4578 by anju (oncall). :lock:
carlos (sre): Thanks. While suppressed, let's route synth checks to fallback region to maintain coverage: update prober config to route eu-west -> eu-central for health checks.
anju (oncall): applying config change (hot reload):
```
kubectl -n synthetic set env deploy/eu-west-prober ROUTE_FALLBACK=eu-central && kubectl rollout restart deploy/eu-west-prober
```
anju (oncall): rollout started. prober logs now show checks succeeding against eu-central health endpoints. green checks coming in on dashboard :white_check_mark:
mei (product): Good. I'll message customer-ops that synthetic health is degraded in eu-west but we've routed checks to fallback and there is no user impact currently.
carlos (sre): I'll pull NAT gateway logs and open an infra ticket. Early signs look like a flapping egress appliance in eu-west-1. If infra confirms, we should add a prober-level dedupe and backoff (increase failure window) to avoid page amplification.
ops-runbook-bot: Suggested followup: create postmortem ticket, tag infra, SRE, and product. Suggested remediation: 1) add 2s jitter to prober retries, 2) implement PD suppression policy for repeated identical synth-check alerts within 10m, 3) failover routing automation.
anju (oncall): PD suppression window expired; re-enabling escalation.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: suppression expired for INC-4578. Escalation active again.
carlos (sre): infra-update: opened INFRA-1221 pointing to NAT gateway cluster node pool. @infra-team please investigate hardware flapping 17:02-17:12 UTC.
mei (product): Noted. I'm creating a tiny customer advisory: "Synthetic checks in eu-west experienced a transient spike; routing moved to fallback. No customer-facing impact." Will post to status.redwood.example in 15m unless infra gives a clean update.
anju (oncall): closing the PD incident as resolved since eu-west prober checks normalized and no new failures for 12m. pdctl close:
```
pdctl incidents resolve INC-4578 --note "prober routed to fallback; NAT gateway flaps observed; infra ticket INFRA-1221 opened"
```
pagerduty-bot: INC-4578 resolved by anju (oncall).
carlos (sre): quick action items (assigned):
- (SRE) add dedupe/backoff config to prober (short-term) -> SRE-TASK-88
- (Infra) investigate NAT hw/flap and add improved NLB health checks -> INFRA-1221
- (Product) publish short advisory + update runbook with suppression guidance -> PROJ-457
mei (product): I'll draft the advisory and the runbook addendum.
anju (oncall): final status: incident-> resolved, no customer impact, fallback routing applied, infra ticket opened. :white_check_mark: Will drop postmortem link when created.
incident-bot: Incident thread closed by anju (oncall). React with :thumbsup: if no follow-up needed."
